name: King Henry VIII
description: Henry VIII, who over the course of the play sheds Cardinal Wolsey, divorces Queen Katherine, and marries Anne Bullen, whose daughter Elizabeth the play ends by celebrating. Shakespeare and Fletcher present him as a king growing into his authority, learning to see through the counsellors who manage him.

name: Cardinal Wolsey
description: Thomas Wolsey, Cardinal and Lord Chancellor, the butcher's son who rose to rule England under the king. He destroys Buckingham, drives the divorce, and amasses vast wealth, until intercepted letters expose his double-dealing and he falls — taking his famous leave of 'all my greatness' and dying humbled at Leicester.

name: Queen Katherine
description: Katherine of Aragon, Henry's first queen, who defends her marriage at the divorce trial with unanswerable dignity ('Sir, I desire you do me right and justice'), refuses to accept the court's authority, and dies in pious exile after a vision of angelic garlands. The play's moral heart.

name: Anne Bullen
description: Anne Bullen (Boleyn), Katherine's maid of honour, who pities the fallen queen even as she supplants her. She becomes Henry's wife and queen, and her coronation and the birth of her daughter Elizabeth crown the play.

name: Duke of Buckingham
description: Edward Stafford, Duke of Buckingham, who denounces Wolsey's pride and is destroyed by him on his own surveyor's perjured testimony. Condemned for treason, he forgives his enemies in a celebrated scaffold speech before his execution.

name: Archbishop Cranmer
description: Thomas Cranmer, Archbishop of Canterbury, who finds for Henry's divorce and is protected by the king from Gardiner's faction. As godfather to the infant Elizabeth he delivers the play's closing prophecy of her glorious reign and that of her successor.

name: Duke of Norfolk
description: Thomas Howard, Duke of Norfolk, a leading noble who warns Buckingham against Wolsey and later helps bring the cardinal down.

name: Duke of Suffolk
description: Charles Brandon, Duke of Suffolk, who joins Norfolk and Surrey in confronting Wolsey at his fall.

name: Earl of Surrey
description: Earl of Surrey, Buckingham's son-in-law, who bitterly upbraids Wolsey to his face once the cardinal has fallen.

name: Lord Chamberlain
description: The Lord Chamberlain, a court official who observes the rise of Anne Bullen and the maneuvers against Cranmer.

name: Bishop Gardiner
description: Stephen Gardiner, Bishop of Winchester and the king's secretary, leader of the conservative faction that tries to bring down Archbishop Cranmer before the council.

name: Thomas Cromwell
description: Wolsey's faithful servant, who weeps at his master's fall and receives his counsel to 'fling away ambition.' He rises in the king's service and defends Cranmer in the council.

name: Cardinal Campeius
description: Cardinal Campeius, the papal legate sent from Rome to sit with Wolsey in judgment on the king's divorce, who adjourns the trial to Rome.

name: Griffith
description: Gentleman usher to Queen Katherine, who attends her in exile and, prompted by her, gives the dead Wolsey a generous and balanced obituary.

name: Old Lady
description: An elderly friend to Anne Bullen, whose worldly, bawdy banter about queenship counterpoints Anne's professed reluctance.

name: First Gentleman
description: One of the Gentlemen whose conversations narrate offstage events — Buckingham's trial, Anne's coronation — serving as the play's choric eyewitnesses.

name: Second Gentleman
description: One of the Gentlemen whose conversations narrate offstage events, supplying the audience with court news and commentary.

name: Third Gentleman
description: A Gentleman who reports the splendor of Anne Bullen's coronation.

name: A Gentleman
description: A gentleman or gentleman-usher delivering messages at court.

name: Lord Chancellor
description: The Lord Chancellor who presides over the council's attempt to commit Cranmer to the Tower.

name: Surveyor
description: Buckingham's discharged surveyor, whose testimony — coached by Wolsey — condemns his former master for treason.

name: Lord Sandys
description: Lord Sandys (Sir William Sandys), a genial courtier at Wolsey's banquet where the king first meets Anne Bullen.

name: Lord Abergavenny
description: Buckingham's son-in-law, arrested with him on Wolsey's orders.

name: Sir Thomas Lovell
description: A courtier in attendance on the king and Wolsey.

name: Brandon
description: An officer who, with a sergeant-at-arms, arrests the Duke of Buckingham for high treason.

name: Capucius
description: Ambassador from the Emperor Charles V, who visits the dying Katherine and carries her last letter to the king.

name: Bishop of Lincoln
description: The Bishop of Lincoln, the king's confessor, who first raised the scruple about the marriage to Katherine.

name: Patience
description: Waiting-woman to Queen Katherine, who attends her in her final illness.

name: Sir Anthony Denny
description: A courtier who brings Archbishop Cranmer to the king at night.

name: Doctor Butts
description: The king's physician, who shows Henry how the council has left Cranmer waiting at the door like a lackey.

name: Secretary
description: A secretary to Cardinal Wolsey.

name: Porter
description: The palace porter who, with his man, struggles to hold back the crowd at the christening of Princess Elizabeth.

name: Porter's Man
description: The porter's man, who helps keep order among the christening crowd.

name: Keeper
description: A keeper at the council chamber door.

name: Crier
description: The court crier who summons the parties at the divorce trial.

name: Scribe
description: A scribe at the legatine court.

name: Messenger
description: A messenger at court.

name: Servant
description: A servant at court.

name: Sergeant-at-Arms
description: A sergeant-at-arms who assists Brandon in arresting Buckingham.

name: Sir Henry Guildford
description: The host who welcomes the guests to Wolsey's banquet.

name: Sir Nicholas Vaux
description: The officer charged with conveying the condemned Buckingham to his execution.

name: Page
description: Page to Bishop Gardiner.

name: Garter King-at-Arms
description: The herald who proclaims good wishes at the christening of Princess Elizabeth.

name: A Voice
description: A voice heard from within.

name: Prologue
description: The speaker of the Prologue, who warns the audience to expect not a merry bawdy play but a serious, tearful 'chosen truth' of greatness brought to misery.

name: Epilogue
description: The speaker of the Epilogue, who guesses the play will please chiefly the good women in the audience, and the men for their sake.

name: Both
description: Two speakers answering together.

name: All
description: Several speakers answering together.
